conflict_topics: Door-closed privacy vs shared access to files
Relocation of active files (storage vs desk)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants gave concrete reasons for their needs (A: scheduled calls, C: daily call to mother's care home, B: active file access), which supported realistic trade-offs.
Practical, localized solution proposed by B (moving active files) rather than abstract bargaining accelerated settlement.
Resolution was explicit and confirmed by each affected party (not merely echoed).
evaluation.final_reason: All parties agreed on concrete adjustments: Agent D will use the small room around 12:30 and 3:30 daily for ~15 minutes with the door closed and a small Buddha statue on the shelf (Agents D and others agreed: Turn10 'So, 12.30 and 3.30 works for me then.'). Agent C gave up the 1:00 slot and accepted 12:30 (Turn9: 'Yeah, 12.30 works.'). Agent A agreed to the 3:30 timing (Turn3: 'Yeah, 3.30 works for me.'). Agent B agreed to move active files out to his desk so that D's closed-door periods will not block urgent file access (Turn6 proposed moving files: 'How about we just move the active files out here by my desk?...' and Turn14 confirmed 'Okay, works for me.'). These mutual, specific acceptances settled the earlier incompatibilities.
position_change_notes: Agent C originally used 1:00 daily but accepted 12:30 instead (Turn7: 'Actually, the 1 p.m. time is a problem for me.' followed by Turn9: 'Yeah, 12.30 works. Thanks.').
Agent A conceded the later 4:30 preference to 3:30 ('Yeah, 3.30 works for me.' — Turn3) to accommodate D's privacy need.

Agent B moved from resistance to the notification plan ('I can't really plan it like that.') to offering a practical accommodation (move active files) and then confirmed acceptance ('Okay, works for me.' — Turn14).

Agent D shifted requested times from 1:00/4:30 to 12:30/3:30 and accepted the file-move solution while insisting on a closed door for the 15-minute intervals ('I need the door to be closed for those fifteen minutes.' — Turn5).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A says the 4:30 time conflicts with calls: 'I often need that room from 4 p.m. onwards for calls with Europe.' Agent D proposes an alternative: 'Could I use it at 3.30 instead?' — a clear scheduling incompatibility appears but is not yet resolved.

Agent A accepts 3:30 ('Yeah, 3.30 works for me.'), but Agent B raises a new, substantive constraint: 'the files I work on are in that room. I have to go in and out to get them all day.' This adds an access-vs-privacy/resource conflict on top of scheduling.

Agent D states a privacy requirement: 'I need the door to be closed for those fifteen minutes.' Agent B resists the proposed notification approach ('I can't really plan it like that') but offers a concrete practical solution: 'How about we just move the active files out here by my desk? Half that stuff in there is for the archive anyway.' The exchange moves toward a practical accommodation, so conflict softens but is not yet fully settled.

Agent C introduces another incompatible use of the 1 p.m. slot: 'Actually, the 1 p.m. time is a problem for me. I use that room every day to call my mother's care home.' This creates a new scheduling conflict over the 1 p.m. time; Agent D proposes 12.30 as an alternative ('What about 12.30?').

Agent C accepts the alternative time ('Yeah, 12.30 works. Thanks.') and Agent D indicates agreement with B's moving-files proposal ('Okay, moving the files sounds good. So, 12.30 and 3.30 works for me then.'). The main remaining open point is explicit confirmation from Agent B that they will move files and accept the new schedule.

Agent B explicitly confirms: 'Okay, works for me.' Agent D responds: 'Great, thanks everyone.' All parties have affirmed the proposed times and the file-move accommodation, resolving the substantive conflicts.

substantive_insights: The main tension was between a user's need for a brief private, closed-door period and another user's need for intermittent, unpredictable access to physical files stored in the same room.
A simple physical rearrangement (moving active files) plus small schedule shifts resolved the incompatibility without requiring heavy policy changes.
Flexible proposals (D offering alternate times and willingness to notify; B proposing file relocation) enabled a mixed compromise/ accommodation solution.
